questions.question: What should you do if you feel tired while driving?

options.text: Stop to rest or let another driver take over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest or let another driver take over.
questions.explanation: Tiredness slows your thinking and reflexes. This makes driving dangerous. Stop and rest or change drivers.

questions.question: What should you do if you are getting tired while driving?

options.text: Stop and rest or switch drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest or switch drivers.
questions.explanation: Take a break every hour on long trips. Share driving with another person so you can both rest.

questions.question: If you drive faster than other cars on a two-lane road and keep passing them, what will happen?

options.text: You will reach your destination much faster and safer.
You will increase your chances of a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will increase your chances of a crash.
questions.explanation: Avoid passing on two-lane roads. Every time you pass, your crash risk goes up.

questions.question: What does a "No passing zone" sign mean?

options.text: It is not safe to pass here.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is not safe to pass here.
questions.explanation: Do not pass in a "No passing zone." This area has limited visibility and passing would be unsafe.

questions.question: In a vehicle with airbags, where is the safest place for children age 12 and under to sit?
questions.correctAnswerText: The back seat.
questions.explanation: Airbags can hurt children. Children age 12 and under must sit in the back seat.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: Wear both parts of a two-part belt. Using only one part does not protect you as well. Even with an automatic shoulder belt, also buckle the lap belt.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through a work zone?

options.text: Follow the car in front of you closely.
Pass the car in front of you as soon as possible.
Keep a safe distance and do not tailgate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance and do not tailgate.
questions.explanation: In work zones, keep space between your car and barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other vehicles. Do not follow too closely.

questions.question: If you are angry after an argument, what should you do?

options.text: Play loud music to stop thinking about it.
Wait a few minutes to calm down before driving.
Drive on the interstate to relieve stress.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait a few minutes to calm down before driving.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions affect your driving. If you are very angry, excited, scared, worried, or sad, calm down first. You need to focus on driving safely.

questions.question: What is the only thing that can reduce blood alcohol content (BAC)?
questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body.

questions.question: What should you do if you see animals near the road while driving?

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and drive carefully.
questions.explanation: Slow down if you see animals near the road. They may suddenly run or change direction. More animals may be nearby that you cannot see.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that people cross here. Stay alert and let pedestrians cross safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turns.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You will often see this sign at intersections with heavy oncoming traffic.

questions.question: If pedestrians cross in the middle of the street instead of at a crosswalk, you:

options.text: Do not have to stop for them.
Should honk your horn at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop for them.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians, even if they are crossing illegally or in the wrong place. Stop for them no matter what.

questions.question: Children on bicycles should be given extra space by drivers because:

options.text: They do not have the same reflexes as adults.
They are smaller and harder to see than adults.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and hard to see. Watch carefully for children near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, parks, and ice cream trucks. Be extra careful when children on bikes might come onto the road from the sidewalk.

questions.question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Keep going. You have the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
Drive around them on the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians cross in a crosswalk. Wait until the intersection is clear before you drive.

questions.question: If you need to stop your car on an interstate, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn to get other drivers' attention.
Get out and flag down the first car that passes.
Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your car if you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your car if you can.
questions.explanation: If you must stop on the shoulder of an interstate or highway, turn on your emergency flashers and stay inside your car. Standing or walking on an interstate is very dangerous because traffic moves so fast.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to process alcohol. Nothing else you do, including eating and drinking, can speed this up.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Merging traffic from the right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to what is coming up ahead. This sign warns you that traffic will merge in from the right, so be ready to make room.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs harm many driving skills, including reaction time, coordination, alertness, and concentration.

questions.question: Reaction time is slower after:
questions.correctAnswerText: Drinking alcohol.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It makes it harder to see clearly and stay alert. The more alcohol in your body, the worse your judgment and driving become. You will have trouble judging distance, speed, and how other vehicles are moving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Get ready. Traffic will merge into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready. Traffic will merge into your lane.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that traffic will enter from the right. Be ready to let them merge safely into your lane.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection:

options.text: You must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.
You never need to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, let oncoming traffic go straight first. Always yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: Blind spots are:

options.text: Areas where your vision gets fuzzy when you are tired.
Parts of the road you cannot see in your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parts of the road you cannot see in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder. Check for anything near the rear corners of your car. These areas are blind spots because your mirrors cannot show them.

questions.question: You should yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
At all times, even if they break traffic laws.
Only if the traffic light is in their favor.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times, even if they break traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Always watch for pedestrians near your vehicle. You must do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter what.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Take a break.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop at a rest area or service station. Nap, stretch, or switch drivers. Caffeine pills and energy drinks cannot replace real rest and may make driving more dangerous.
